scenario: [LIMP.12.2]: `CallError` is written into the artefact whenever the program contains a `call` action, whether or not a rule matches it, because an adapter may assert one for any call ([LCRS.4.2.2], [LCRS.17.1]). The program calls the `no response` service `svc.ping`, has no continuation, and no rule names `CallError`. The host asserts a `CallError` (corr, code, message, ts) as an adapter would, and it is accepted: one fact is live. Rule `r` is there only so the program contains a `call`; no `Job` is asserted, so it never fires ([RCTS.1.2.17]). PATH PINNED: `dsc.driver`'s `limp_12_2_call_uses`, which writes the built-in `CallError` for any `call`; libds's `ds_engine_assert` (through pyds, runner.py) and the Mercury runtime's `host_assert` (test_behave.m) look the schema up in the loaded artefact. Break: a compiler that writes `CallError` only when a pattern or a continuation names it leaves it out, and both runtimes refuse the assert with DS_ERR_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN.
rules_ds:
service svc.ping:
    kwarg n: Int
    no response

schema Job scope explicit:
    id: Int

rule r:
    Job j
->
    call svc.ping n: j.id nocooldown
